headline: Broad market dip as geopolitical tensions weigh on sentiment
deck: All three major indices fell between 0.46% and 0.65% as Middle East tensions and Fed expectations keep investors on edge.
body:
Equity markets retreated across the board this morning, with the Nasdaq leading losses at -0.65% followed by the Dow at -0.62% and the S&P 500 at -0.46%. The broad decline mirrors investor caution around multiple geopolitical flashpoints: ongoing US-Houthi diplomatic engagement, escalating US sanctions discussions toward Russia, and rising China-US tensions over military "provocative acts." These headline risks are compounded by the Strait of Hormuz shipping slowdown, which could have supply chain implications if escalation continues.

On the fixed-income side, the 10-year Treasury held steady just below 5% at 4.97%, reflecting a market still caught between growth concerns and expectations around the Fed's next policy decision. The near-flat move in yields suggests investors are hedging bets—neither fully pricing in rate cuts nor expecting aggressive tightening, leaving bonds and equities in a holding pattern. With earnings season winding down and macro uncertainty elevated, market momentum appears subdued.

On the positive note, Boeing's finalization of a 103-aircraft order with Korean Air and a J.D. Power report showing improved passenger satisfaction at US airports provided modest tailwinds to sentiment. However, these constructive signals were insufficient to overcome the weight of geopolitical headlines and Fed uncertainty, leaving the market to close out the day in the red.
